newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan pins hopes on new Hong Kong leader.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan pins hopes on new Hong Kong leader.

text.p: Taiwan said on Wednesday it believed Hong Kong's chief executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa would play a positive role in bilateral relations when he assumes his post after the British colony returns to China next July.

"We believe he (Tung) can play a positive role in promoting future relations between Taiwan and Hong Kong," state radio quoted William Li, director of the Mainland Affairs Council's Hong Kong and Macau affairs department, as saying.
The cabinet-level council oversees Taiwan's policy toward China.
Tung won a historic vote on Wednesday and will become Hong Kong's first Chinese leader when more than 150 years of British rule ends in mid-1997.
The magnate's shipping background and familiarity with Taiwan should help promote relations between Taiwan and China after the 1997 handover, the radio quoted Li as saying.
Taiwan has banned direct contact with China since a 1949 civil war and all direct exchanges, including shipping, must be conducted through a third region, mostly Hong Kong.
Taiwan has said it would regard Hong Kong as a special territory different from the Chinese mainland after 1997, maintaining Taipei's ban on direct contact with China.

Tung has said in public that he would promote Hong Kong as a bridge between rival Taiwan and China and "that complies with the policy of the Republic of China government (in Taiwan)," Li said. The British colony's handover to China is widely seen as a step toward Taiwan's own reunification with the mainland, something both sides espouse, though under very different terms.
Taiwan insists that reunification can only be realised when China -- like the Nationalist-ruled island itself -- becomes democratic.

China has promised to let Hong Kong keep its capitalist system for 50 years under a "one country, two systems" model in what many experts believe is a test run for Beijing's bigger aim of bringing Taiwan under its sovereignty.
